bottom_line: In patients undergoing PCI for acute coronary syndromes, double-dose clopidogrel reduced cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke at 30 days versus standard-dose clopidogrel (adjusted hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.74–0.99).
implications: In this prespecified PCI subgroup, the reported 30-day data support that double-dose clopidogrel (vs standard-dose) was associated with a lower absolute event rate for cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (3.9% vs 4.5%) with an adjusted HR of 0.86 (95% CI 0.74–0.99), alongside a higher major bleeding rate (1.6% vs 1.1%). The aspirin dose comparison shows similar primary-outcome rates (4.1% vs 4.2%) with an adjusted HR of 0.98 (0.84–1.13), and therefore does not support a difference in the primary composite outcome between high-dose and low-dose aspirin over 30 days in this PCI population.

major_points.text: Double-dose clopidogrel reduced the 30-day primary composite outcome compared with standard-dose clopidogrel.
major_points.quote: Compared with the standard dose, double-dose clopidogrel reduced the rate of the primary outcome (330 events [3·9%] vs 392 events [4·5%]; adjusted hazard ratio 0·86, 95% CI 0·74–0·99, p=0·039)

major_points.text: High-dose versus low-dose aspirin did not differ for the primary outcome.
major_points.quote: High-dose and low-dose aspirin did not diﬀer for the primary outcome (356 [4·1%] vs 366 [4·2%]; 0·98, 0·84–1·13, p=0·76).

major_points.text: Major bleeding was more common with double-dose than with standard-dose clopidogrel.
major_points.quote: Major bleeding was more common with double-dose than with standard-dose clopidogrel (139 [1·6%] vs 99 [1·1%]; 1·41, 1·09–1·83, p=0·009)

major_points.text: Clopidogrel comparison was double-blind; aspirin comparison was open label with blinded outcome assessment.
major_points.quote: The clopidogrel dose comparison was double-blind and the aspirin dose comparison was open label with blinded assessment of outcomes.

absolute_effects.text: Primary outcome (CV death, MI, or stroke) at 30 days: 330 (3.9%) vs 392 (4.5%).

subgroups.quote: There was consistency in the treatment eﬀect for each dose comparison in predeﬁned subgroups (ﬁgure 4B).

subgroups.text: Consistent effects recorded in STEMI and non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndromes.

harms.text: Major bleeding was more common with double-dose than standard-dose clopidogrel.
